name: Basilic Fly Studio Limited
summary: Global VFX delivery access is real, but capitalized development, old receivables and conflicting financial reconciliations weaken the earnings-to-cash bridge. Complete conditional annual models are provided; investment ranking remains on a specific reliability hold.

score_note: BQS/GQS are NS because REV lacks a comparable organic historical anchor. IAS is NS because Q/R/P are unsupported; model calculations and evidence-backed weaker factors remain visible. No missing factor is replaced by a midpoint.

gates.reason: Disclosed approvals and small identified compliance lapses are weighed alongside pledge/remuneration concerns. No evidenced severe integrity failure is asserted.

Face P&L/EPS attribution, transition profit/cash-flow presentations, FX cash-flow sign and gratuity-note balances do not fully reconcile. Capitalization and minority-value normalization remain material.

Reference schedule funds investment without new borrowing under its assumptions; bear requires refinancing/new debt and fails the cash floor without it. Deposit release, project spending and unquantified acquisition claims remain conditional, not guaranteed facilities.
Official 60-session data support a calculable exit test, but lots, ASM/caution flags and missing live-depth information restrict implementation. Migration is not yet verified complete.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Basilic is an established project-based VFX group, not a recurring-revenue software platform. Global delivery access and the One of Us acquisition support a larger opportunity, but ₹59.7 crore development capitalization, old receivables and inconsistent financial-note bridges prevent a reliability-cleared investment ranking. Complete conditional models give bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹3.99/₹335.67/₹934.13, against the official 19 October 2026 close ₹200.65. These are assumptions-dependent scenarios, not three verified fair values. The base annualized return is 12.27% over the dated holding period, below the 15% analytical hurdle. [S1] [S17] [S90]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Evidence-backed factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, DUR 5, CAP 3, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 4 and EARN 3, each Medium confidence. REV is NS because acquisition/GAAP changes prevent the required comparable historical anchor. BQS and GQS remain NS with original weights and explicit bounds; persistent CASH 3 caps GQS at 5. IAS retains D 2 and L 5 but Q/R/P are NS. The financial model is complete: missing R/P reflects normalization uncertainty, not an omitted calculation. No historical score 9–10 is claimed on a short or Medium-confidence record. Gates exclude investment ranking without erasing the weaker factors that can be assessed. [S1] [S3] [S4] [S5] [S17] [S90]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Basilic supplies visual effects, compositing and related post-production through India and overseas studios. Contracts and artist effort drive revenue; project timing, revisions and collection acceptance matter more than a software-style recurring subscription base. India retains substantial subcontracting exposure to other studios, while overseas operations provide direct production-house access. One of Us was acquired through the UK subsidiary in July 2024, adding UK/Paris capabilities. FY2026 AOC-1 reports Canada ownership 90.63%, UK 100%, One of Us UK 70% via the UK subsidiary and Paris 75% via One of Us, implying 52.5% effective Paris ownership. Subsidiary turnover cannot be simply added because intercompany eliminations and possible sub-group scope differ. [S1] [S4] [S17]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Established customer access, creative execution and the ability to share work across locations support an ordinary-to-moderate service advantage. CRISIL explicitly recognizes the operating network while highlighting technology obsolescence and working-capital demands. Neither prominent production credits nor acquired awards establish pricing power. AI/rendering improvements can lower cost, but may also reduce billable effort or increase competition. As a historical peer check, Phantom Digital Effects FY2025 consolidated revenue was ₹102.1579 crore, PAT ₹20.2021 crore and CFO −₹18.8084 crore. Its strict EBITDA of ₹37.4793 crore, about 36.69% of revenue, therefore does not establish superior cash economics. Different periods, acquisitions and capitalization prevent importing a current peer multiple. The scenario multiples are explicit analyst assumptions, not a claimed market consensus. [S5] [S17] [S19]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Original FY2023/FY2024 revenue was ₹78.6674/₹102.6697 crore. FY2025 original operating revenue ₹304.09 crore rounds to the FY2026 comparative ₹304.1 crore; the approximately ₹306.1 crore original total-income figure is not operating revenue; FY2026 revenue is ₹407.8 crore, a reported 34.1% increase. July 2024 acquisition timing makes FY2025 partial-year versus FY2026 full-year One of Us consolidation material. A nominal three-year CAGR across that break would overstate evidence for organic growth. Standalone revenue ₹70.2273/₹100.3005/₹73.55/₹120.4 crore in FY2023–26 implies roughly 19.7% CAGR, but FY2026 disclosed service income from group companies totals ₹34.9 crore versus ₹14.7 crore previously. It is therefore not a clean substitute for group external organic growth. June-quarter FY2027 revenue ₹103.5 crore rose 9.9%, but operating EBITDA fell from ₹18.6 to ₹14.4 crore and PAT from ₹12.0 to ₹6.7 crore; reported diluted EPS fell from ₹5.16 to ₹2.61. This is contrary evidence to a simple high-growth extrapolation. Customer producer/studio split and group organic volumes remain insufficiently reconciled for REV. [S1] [S3] [S4] [S14] [S17]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The Bengaluru 150-seat target and offshore transfer of high-end work offer an execution path, not achieved incremental returns. Shareholders approved an IPO-object variation using approximately ₹21.4 crore unspent proceeds plus ₹1.9 crore other resources toward a ₹23.3 crore plan, with March 2027 as the milestone. Management describes roughly ₹700 crore pipeline opportunities, including advanced discussions; the whole amount is not a contracted order book. June guidance for another ₹15–20 crore technology investment can overlap or supplement that plan, so the model includes both interpretations. FY2026 cash-rent-adjusted ROIC proxy is 17.44%, but incremental NOPAT/financing capital is about 6.31%; economically expensing the ₹59.7 crore development spend reduces the current ROIC sensitivity to about 1.22%. Goodwill and development remain in invested capital. Acquisition/transition scope prevents describing these as clean organic lifetime returns. [S1] [S2] [S13] [S17]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The ₹85 crore gross QIP and disclosed shareholder approvals show access to funding and formal decision processes. The September 2025 placement document separately discloses promoter share pledges for promoter borrowings; its amount and subsequent release are not inferred from a later inactive exchange caution. July 2026 notices seek approval for cross-border director offices/remuneration, including reimbursement mechanics, which warrants monitoring rather than automatic misconduct attribution. The FY2026 secretarial report records an ₹11,000 NSE penalty for an 11-day XBRL investor-grievance filing delay despite timely PDF submission, paid within the notice period. It also records a designated person trading without preclearance and a ₹15,000 company-imposed penalty remitted to the SEBI-administered fund, with reporting to exchanges on 3 February 2026. These are specific historical compliance findings, not evidence of fraud, a current suspension or severe minority abuse. Current auditor statements do not erase the identified financial reconciliation questions. [S1] [S15] [S16] [S18]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Cash conversion: FY2024 CFO was −₹27.9028 crore; FY2025 original CFO ₹9.63 crore, the transition table ₹19.8 crore and the latest comparative ₹20.0 crore. FY2026 CFO ₹22.9 crore is 0.453× group PAT. On the latest two-year comparatives, CFO/PAT is 0.450×, not a mixed-GAAP long-term ratio. FY2026 capex/development cash ₹73.0 crore, debt interest ₹8.5 crore and lease cash ₹8.5 crore leave −₹67.1 crore after those uses. Receivables consume ₹67.4 crore in the cash-flow statement. Gross AR aged over one year totals ₹43.5 crore versus only ₹0.8 crore ECL. Management collection claims partly discuss standalone balances including intercompany receivables; they do not independently establish a subsequent consolidated AR balance.

Normalization: strict EBITDA is ₹82.0 crore after severance; deducting full lease cash gives ₹73.5 crore. Another ₹59.7 crore went into unamortized development, leaving ₹13.8 crore before other investment, working capital and financing. The June transcript explicitly identifies mixed internal employee and external costs; no claim is made that all development is payroll or improper capitalization. Models capitalize future spending, amortize it, and separately normalize terminal sustaining-development costs.

Specific reliability issues remain: FY2025 transition profit/CF do not fully bridge to the main comparative presentation; the FY2026 EPS note labels group PAT ₹50.6 crore as owners profit although the face P&L assigns owners ₹48.8 crore; the cash flow adds ₹7.3 crore FX “gain/loss” while other income reports the same positive amount; aggregate gratuity provisions ₹3.5 crore exceed the actuarial net obligation ₹2.3 crore. A mechanical FX sign reversal would alter CFO by ₹14.6 crore, but is a reconciliation sensitivity, not an asserted corrected issuer figure. No source is silently changed.

Opening claims: ₹187.8 crore operating WC includes salaries/expenses, statutory accruals and customer advances. Tax ₹20.5 crore and current gratuity ₹0.1 crore settle once separately. NC gratuity ₹3.4 crore is a terminal claim, with a ₹2.2 crore alternative consistent with the smaller actuarial total; future service costs are already funded in operating expenses. Government balances ₹14 crore stay within WC, not also offset against taxes. All ₹64.7 crore debt includes ₹38.4 crore current maturities. Leases are handled through cash rent with no duplicate terminal lease liability. No separately quantified acquisition/put payable was established in reviewed sources, so an additional ₹10 crore claim sensitivity is retained rather than declaring none exists. [S1] [S3] [S4] [S13] [S17]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The five-year annual schedules run FY2027–FY2031 from March 2026 opening balances, with the return clock from 19 October 2026 to 31 March 2031 (4.446 years). This timing mismatch and missing interim balance sheet limit precision. Reference growth is 8/10/10/8/8%, cash-rent-adjusted EBITDA margin 18%, development cash 4.5% of revenue, physical capex 3%, operating WC 46%, debt interest 11% and tax 25%. First-year total investment is at least ₹23.3 crore. New development uses a five-year amortization assumption; the terminal multiple of 12 applies to EBITDA after cash rent, physical depreciation and recurring development cash spend, avoiding an artificial amortization-expiry gain.

Debt, cash, current/NC legacy claims and minority equity value are explicitly linked. Reference minority participation is an analyst 10% group-equity proxy; observed FY2026 profit-share 3.56% and 20% cases are not claimed to equal contractual forward rights. Current deposits are assumed usable on maturity for authorized spending/refinancing, with ₹17 crore and all ₹29.4 crore deferred-release cases. Excluded deposits remain terminal assets, not written off. Reference terminal price is ₹335.67, annualized return 12.27%; it requires no new debt under its assumptions, but adverse cases do. The model includes half-year draw and maturity interest, cash identities, DCF sensitivities, hurdle-entry prices and margin/multiple grids. Keeping other assumptions fixed, 8% development cash spending gives ₹210.90 terminal value, a 14% cash-rent-adjusted margin ₹198.92, 55% working capital ₹312.05, 20% minority participation ₹298.37, and a separate additional ₹23.3 crore buildout ₹318.55. Full current-deposit deferral gives ₹333.78 and requires ₹11.86 crore new borrowing, rather than treating those deposits as permanently lost. Sustainable capitalization economics and minority/financial-note reconciliation still make R/P NS. [S1] [S5] [S13] [S14] [S17] [S90]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Bear assumptions are flat revenue for two years then 3% growth, 12% cash-rent-adjusted margin, 6% development cash, 3.5% physical capex, 55% WC, 13% interest, 8× terminal economic EBIT and 20% minority participation. A ₹18.435 crore analyst loss on old receivables/prepaids reduces opening recoverable WC; replacement funding enters delta-WC once. A ₹23.25 crore goodwill impairment is noncash and is not subtracted again from earnings-based enterprise value. No immediate tax credit is assumed. The bear requires ₹138.03 crore of conditional new borrowing/refinancing and yields ₹3.99 per share, about 98.0% below entry. Without new debt its cash-floor test fails, so that case has no feasible return label. The path is delayed collections plus development/overseas cost commitments, not merely a lower P/E. [S1] [S17] [S90]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Reverse calculations hold the reference cost/WC/terminal assumptions fixed and solve for revenue growth, not a promised outcome. A 15% return requires terminal price ₹373.52 and about 11.78% annual revenue growth under fixed reference assumptions. Fivefold value requires about 41.03% growth, terminal revenue ₹2,275.05 crore, cumulative investment ₹481.37 crore and conditional borrowing ₹516.04 crore. Tenfold value requires about 63.49% growth, terminal revenue ₹4,762.93 crore, investment ₹841.12 crore and borrowing ₹1,462.62 crore. Those requirements expose the strain of maintaining margins while expanding a talent-intensive business. These are not supported by the disclosed pipeline alone. Future acquisitions, further dilution, delivery capacity and collection funding would change the result; none is treated as free. [S1] [S13] [S17] [S90]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: First seek a single issuer bridge for transition/group/owner PAT, EPS, the FX cash-flow adjustment and gratuity balances. Track actual group collections and >1-year AR against the June/August claims, rather than standalone/intercompany aggregates. Check development commissioning, useful lives, cash spend and any impairments, then compare achieved incremental returns with the cost of capital. Verify Bengaluru completion/use of IPO funds by March 2027, QIP utilization, any signed acquisition with full consideration/claims and ownership, and promoter-pledge changes. For implementation, refresh actual migration notices, Stage I/other surveillance, board lot, spreads and order-book depth; 60 historical trading sessions do not guarantee a future exit. [S1] [S2] [S11] [S13] [S17] [S18] [S95] [S96]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: completed conditional-model review with an unresolved financial-reliability hold. It is neither a cleared investment candidate nor a finding of wrongdoing. Existing operations support several ordinary/weak quality scores; the unresolved historical growth anchor prevents full BQS/GQS, and normalization prevents IAS. A dated quote and completed annual scenarios do not cure those factual gaps. Reconsider the classification only after reconciled accounts, development/ownership economics and refreshed funding/implementation evidence, not simply after a price decline. [S1] [S17] [S90]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual reports FY2024–FY2026, the September 2025 placement document, 2026 exchange filings and two earnings calls were reviewed alongside the dated CRISIL rationale and official NSE market/security/surveillance data. Annual-report read status is partial because relevant sections, not every boilerplate page, were reviewed. Phantom is a dated FY2025 operating/cash comparator, not an independently verified current valuation benchmark. Figures use crore unless stated; source million values are divided by ten. Model margins, taxes, growth, useful lives, minority participation and terminal multiples are analyst assumptions with sensitivities. Important unresolved questions are historical reconciliation, intangible project recoverability, forward ownership/claims, exact deposit encumbrance/release and subsequent group collections. Source-disclosed nil commitments/contingencies do not prove that every possible future claim is zero. [S1] [S3] [S4] [S5] [S18] [S19]

liquidity.implementation_assessment: All 60 sessions observed.₹5 lakh sale at2/5/10% of lower60-session mean/median takes8.384/3.353/1.677 sessions before spread, impact, queues and circuit limits. This is a turnover proxy, not an execution promise.

GOV.reason: Disclosure of shareholder approvals, financing and remuneration provides traceability. Contrary: promoter-pledge exposure and financial-note inconsistencies lower stewardship confidence; small documented compliance penalties are not evidence of fraud or severe minority abuse.

MOAT.reason: Multi-location creative talent and established studio relationships support client access. Contrary: project-based economics, technology obsolescence and Q1 margin pressure do not show durable pricing power; credits and awards are not a monopoly.

REV.reason: The reported 34.1% FY26 increase is real as disclosed, but partial-to-full-year One of Us consolidation and GAAP changes prevent a defensible organic multi-year anchor. Standalone FY2023–26 growth is a useful cross-check but includes increasing intragroup service revenue, so it cannot substitute for the missing group organic anchor.

DUR.reason: Cross-border production access and Bengaluru/offshore expansion support a runway. Contrary: the roughly₹700 crore pipeline includes opportunities, not all contracts; funding, AI pricing and integration constrain realizable duration.

CAP.reason: Goodwill and development are retained in the financing-capital proxy; incremental return is about 6.31%, below a 12–16% cost-of-capital range. Contrary: reported cash-rent-adjusted ROIC is 17.44% and development may create future benefits, but the expensing sensitivity is only 1.22% and project returns are unproven.

CASH.reason: Negative FY24 CFO and weak subsequent CFO/PAT, aged receivables and₹67.1 crore FY26 cash deficit after reinvestment/financing support persistent weakness. Contrary: FY26 CFO is positive and management reports collections, but these do not establish comparable group realization.

BAL.reason: ₹73.9 crore cash/current deposits versus₹64.7 crore debt and a financed conditional base provide capacity. Contrary: deposits have collateral-use uncertainty,₹20.6 crore legacy current claims, development spending and adverse scenarios requiring new credit; rated proposed limits are not cash.

EXEC.reason: The overseas acquisition and delivery network are operational and QIP funding completed. Contrary: receivable clean-up is not independently quantified at group level, integration margins weakened in Q1 and the March2027 Bengaluru milestone is still future.

EARN.reason: Owners FY26 PAT is₹48.8 crore, or₹19.31 on current shares, versus₹15.71 on prior shares. Contrary to that improvement, unamortized development exceeds owners PAT and Q1 reported EPS falls 49.4%; the face-P&L/earnings-note inconsistency prevents treating reported EPS as clean cash earnings.

R.reason: Returns are calculated, not withheld. The true normalized development burden, minority distributable-value split and contradictory historical profit/cash-flow/benefit disclosures leave the reference return too uncertain for a scored investment case.

D.reason: The bear model loses about98% of entry value and needs substantial conditional borrowing; no-new-credit bear breaches the cash floor. Aged receivables and intangible recovery are correlated downside risks. Contrary: current liquidity and the base cash schedule provide some cushion.

P.reason: Reverse hurdle,5×/10× and multiple/margin grids are computed. The price-expectation score remains NS because the sustainable economic earnings and minority claim base are not reliably established, not because calculations were omitted.

L.reason: The quantitative60-session test starts at7 for 3.35 sessions at5% participation. A two-point caution reflects the ₹60,195 lot, short-term ASM Stage I, less-than100-PAN/market-making-ended flags and unknown live depth. All 60 sessions are observed; exchange irregular-SME wording does not imply invented zero-volume days.
